title: Ventana manufacturing latency-bucket synthesis and cost sensitivity
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures the benchmarking we ran for Ventana Manufacturing's POC (June 2027). Objective: characterize latency buckets across expected request profiles, measure throughput under concurrency, and produce a cost-sensitivity matrix to inform a deployment recommendation (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). This is a working synthesis from a two-day workshop and a 36-hour stress sweep on Redwood Dedicated hardware.

Key takeaways:
- For short prompt workflows (avg input tokens ~20, output ~40): P95 latency target of <120ms is achievable with a quantized 13B variant on H100-backed Dedicated pool with continuous batching configured to 40ms window. P99 sits ~220ms.
- For long-form generation (avg input 120 tokens, output 512 tokens): end-to-end P95 is driven by model decode time and KV cache reuse; Dedicated + prefix caching reduced cost by ~26% and P95 by ~18% over stateless Hosted runs.
- Cost sensitivity: moving from FP16 -> 4-bit quantization reduces token cost by 45% for throughput-bound workloads with <2% measured quality regressions on Ventana eval prompts.
- Autoscale recommendations: scale policy keyed to 95th pct incoming QPS with steady-state buffer of 30% headroom and a fast-burst lane (burst pool) for microbursts.

POC scope and assumptions:
- Customer: Ventana Manufacturing (assembly-line SOP assistant and QA checklist summarization).
- Traffic profile provided by customer: predominant synchronous chat API calls (70%), batch classification jobs (20%), embeddings for search (10%).
- Peak QPS target for POC: 220 rps sustained for 10 minutes, microbursts up to 800 rps for <60s.
- SLO target: P95 latency <250ms for chat flows, availability 99.9% during business hours.

Testbed details:
- Redwood runtime: release v2.8.3 (serving runtime + smart-routing fixes).
- Hardware: Dedicated pool variants: (A) 4x H100-80GB nodes (NVIDIA H100), (B) 8x A100-40GB nodes (backpressure config).
- Model variants tested: rw-redwood-14b-v1 fp16, rw-redwood-14b-v1-4bit, llama-2-13b-chat fp16, mistral-7b-instruct fp16.
- Quantization: Post-training static 4-bit quant (Redwood quant-pipeline v1.4).
- Autoscaling policy baseline: target_util=0.63, cool_down=90s, scale_step=1 node. Burst lane implemented as a small pre-warmed A100 cluster.
- Workloads: 1) short-chat (S): in=20, out=40 tokens, 2) long-gen (L): in=120, out=512 tokens, 3) batch-embed (E): 512 texts per batch.

Synthetic harness and measurement method:
- Each workload run for 30 minutes at target concurrency levels with 3 warmup minutes discarded.
- Measurements: P50/P95/P99 latency (ms) for end-to-end response, decode tokens/sec, requests/sec, GPU utilization (nvidia-smi sampling), memory footprint, and cost estimator (tokens * per-token unit rate + infra amortization).
- Quality checks: 200 sample prompts from Ventana's private prompt set evaluated for semantic preservation when using quantized models (BLEU-like and manual spot checks).

Results: short-chat (S)
- H100 pool, rw-redwood-14b-v1 fp16, batching window 40ms, batch size avg 12: P50=42ms, P95=95ms, P99=180ms, throughput=280 rps, tokens/sec ~44k, GPU util 72%
- H100 pool, 4-bit quant, batching window 40ms, batch size avg 18: P50=36ms, P95=110ms, P99=210ms, throughput=420 rps, tokens/sec ~68k, GPU util 88%
- A100 pool, fp16, batching window 60ms, avg batch 10: P50=55ms, P95=140ms, P99=300ms, throughput=210 rps
- Notes: quantized runs achieved higher throughput at cost of modestly higher P95/P99 tail due to increased decode variability with 4-bit kernels.

Results: long-gen (L)
- H100 fp16, KV caching disabled: P50=520ms, P95=1,480ms, P99=2,050ms for 512-token outputs at concurrency 8
- H100 fp16, KV caching enabled (per-session): P50=410ms, P95=1,120ms, P99=1,760ms; tokens/sec +22%
- H100 4-bit quant, KV caching enabled: P50=430ms, P95=1,340ms, P99=1,950ms; small quality diffs on code-like prompts in 6/200 samples
- Notes: long-form performance dominated by per-token decode; KV cache critical when prompt reuse occurs (common for Ventana SOP summarization where seed context reappears).

Results: batch-embed (E)
- A100 fp16, batched embeddings 512 items/batch: throughput 10k embeddings/sec, end-to-end P95 ~220ms for the batch (amortized per-item ~0.022ms), cost-per-embedding favorable on A100 pool.

Cost sensitivity matrix (approx pre-negotiation):
- Hosted (shared pool, fp16): baseline cost estimate for target steady-state load ~ $4,200/day for chat + embeddings (excludes enterprise discounts).
- Dedicated H100 fp16 pool (provisioned for 220 rps steady): infra amortized cost ~ $2,900/day + unit model runtime tokens cost -> effective per-token ~0.00085 USD
- Dedicated H100 4-bit: infra cost similar but effective per-token drops ~45% -> per-token ~0.00047 USD. Net daily ~ $1,700/day (with same request profile).
- Private on-prem (customer provided H100): marginal Redwood fee + support ~ $1,200/day equivalent (model hosting and control plane) but operational overhead on Ventana for infra and SRE.

Interpretation and tradeoffs:
- If Ventana's primary driver is predictable latency (tight P95) and low ops overhead, Dedicated H100 fp16 with well-tuned batching and KV cache is the sweet spot.
- If cost is critical and load is throughput bound (>15k tokens/sec), then moving to 4-bit quantized model on Dedicated delivers large cost reductions with acceptable quality tradeoffs on our test set.
- Hosted is quickest to trial but less predictable for tail SLOs during customer microbursts; fallback policies and smart routing reduce impact but do not match Dedicated predictability.

Operational recommendations (deployment proposal):
1) Minimal Dedicated staging: 3x H100 nodes + 1x A100 burst node. Configure continuous batching (40ms window) for chat routes, enable per-session KV cache for long-gen routes, enable response streaming for >128 token outputs.
2) Autoscale policy: target_util=0.65, min_nodes=3, max_nodes=12, burst_lane_nodes=2 (A100), scale_cooldown=60s.
3) Model config: ship rw-redwood-14b-v1-4bit as the cost-optimized default for chat with an fp16 variant for prioritized customers/paths; rollout via canary (2% -> 10% -> 100%) and monitor quality regressions using Redwood Optimize eval hooks.
4) Observability: enable per-route token-level cost telemetry, P95/P99 tail alerts, and latent-decode anomaly detection. Backfill 7 days of traces into the Console to calibrate thresholds.
5) Runbook snippets:
   - If P95 rises >20%: check batch window fullness, backpressure events, GPU mem pressure; temporarily spawn A100 burst nodes and lower batching window to 25ms.
   - If P99 tail flares without util rise: isolate specific request templates via tracing, apply per-template caching or guardrails, and consider routing to fp16 fallback models.

Quality/regen checks:
- 4-bit quant produced semantic drift in 3% of Ventana's code-like examples and 1.2% of SOP summaries. Recommend a short human-in-the-loop review period for the first 48 hours of production traffic on the quant variant.

Open questions for Ventana:
- How much burst capacity SLA do you want beyond 800 rps? (affects reserved nodes/burst lane sizing)
- Tolerance for 2–4% semantic regression on quantized runs; acceptable for internal QA but not for external customer-facing outputs?
- On-prem acceptance: does Ventana want Redwood-managed control plane or self-hosted entirely?

Next steps (proposed timeline):
- Week 0: finalize model choice and sign Dedicated term sheet for a 30-day trial.
- Week 1: deploy staging Dedicated pool (3x H100 + 1x A100 burst), configure routing and KV caches, smoke tests.
- Week 2: run production-like sweep for 72 hours, collect cost telemetry and quality evals.
- Week 3: review results, lock autoscale params, schedule go/no-go for pilot.

Appendix: quick tables (abbrev)
- Topline numbers (chat short): H100 fp16 P95=95ms, H100 4-bit P95=110ms (throughput +50%)
- Cost delta: 4-bit vs fp16 ~ -45% token cost
- Recommended initial Dedicated: 3x H100, 1x A100 burst, quantized default with fp16 fallback route

Notes to self and team:
- Follow up with infra on persistent kernel variance observed in 4-bit loads (see JIRA-SE-4821).
- Add Ventana's 200 prompt eval to Redwood Optimize as a canonical check for future rollouts.
- Prepare a short customer one-pager summarizing the tradeoffs (cost vs latency vs quality) for the upcoming customer call.

End of synthesis.
